md: The ring spins while it waits, burning a whole CPU. Real shared-memory queues sleep when empty or full, for example on a POSIX semaphore placed in the shared region, as shm_overview(7) suggests, and use spinning at most for a short time first.

courseTitle: Tail latency (p99, p99.9) and coordinated omission
lessonTitle: Coordinated omission: the load tester stops looking when it hurts
md: Coordinated omission does not make individual samples wrong: the 2 ms readings were real. The bug is which samples exist. The tester samples less often precisely when the server is slow, so the sample set is biased toward good moments. No statistic computed afterwards can recover samples that were never taken.

courseTitle: Telecom and satellite security: SS7, SIM swapping, 5G and space links
lessonTitle: IMSI catchers and false base stations: downgrade and detection
md: Turning on 5G does not remove the 2G risk by itself. As long as the phone will still accept 2G, an attacker can try to push it there. Disabling 2G on the device is what closes the fallback.

courseTitle: Telecom and satellite security: SS7, SIM swapping, 5G and space links
lessonTitle: Case: the Viasat KA-SAT attack (24 February 2022)
md: KA-SAT was hit through its ground segment: a VPN appliance, a trusted management network and legitimate commands sent at scale. Protect the management plane like the product itself, and limit how much any single command can break.

courseTitle: Temporal reasoning: years of experience and current roles
lessonTitle: Allen relations, current roles and time-scoped queries
md: Every time-scoped question becomes interval arithmetic once two things are fixed: the reference date, and the convention for partial dates. Allen relations, current-role tests and window clipping are all a few endpoint comparisons.

courseTitle: Test-time compute scaling: sampling, search and thinking longer
lessonTitle: Verifiers set the ceiling: error rates, GenRM and self-verification
md: Self-verification is not free precision. The same paper finds that frontier models have remarkably weak verification out of the box and needed these prompting strategies (and introduces a benchmark for it). Before scaling N, measure your verifier's true and false positive rates on your own samples.

courseTitle: Test-time compute scaling: sampling, search and thinking longer
lessonTitle: Measure it yourself: a test-time scaling harness on GSM8K
md: A scaling harness is three numbers per question and $k$: coverage, what your selection rule achieves, and the gap between them, split by difficulty. The gap tells you how much a better verifier could buy; the bins tell you where to spend the budget.

courseTitle: Test-time training and learned memory: TTT layers and Titans
lessonTitle: Large-chunk TTT, one map of the design space, and the costs
md: Learned memory turns the state of a recurrent layer into a model trained online. You choose its architecture, objective, forgetting and optimizer; you pay for expressiveness in wall-clock time, and you still pair it with attention for exact local recall.

courseTitle: Threat hunting
lessonTitle: Three ways to start a hunt: hypothesis, intelligence and data
md: A hypothesis that cannot fail is not a hypothesis. "Something bad may be happening somewhere" will consume a week and conclude nothing. Name the behaviour, the place and the data. A disproved hypothesis is a useful result: it is evidence that one specific attack path is not in use, at least in the data you have.

courseTitle: Cyber threat intelligence
lessonTitle: What threat intelligence is, and what it is for
md: Threat intelligence is threat information that has been analysed and put in context **for a decision**. If you cannot name the decision a product supports, you are not yet producing intelligence.

courseTitle: Cyber threat intelligence
lessonTitle: Sharing at machine speed: TAXII, MISP and communities
md: Automated sharing amplifies errors as fast as it spreads truth. Before publishing, check values against warning lists, set `to_ids` only on values safe to block, add an expiry or decay model, and never publish an indicator you have not graded.

courseTitle: Thinking like an attacker: threat models and security principles
lessonTitle: STRIDE per element: from a diagram to a threat list
md: STRIDE per element checks parts, not their combination. The 2006 article admits that threats frequently materialise only when systems are joined, because combining them violates assumptions each part made. Always ask what changes when this system is connected to the next one.

courseTitle: Tiered memory: placing pages across DRAM, CXL and SSD
lessonTitle: Why memory is becoming a hierarchy of tiers
md: Tiering wins only if the *hot* pages live in the fast tier. The capacity of each tier matters less than the fraction of accesses it serves. Everything in this course is machinery for keeping $h$ high cheaply.

courseTitle: Time-series forecasting: baselines, smoothing and honest backtests
lessonTitle: Honest evaluation: error metrics, MASE and rolling origins
md: Report a forecast's accuracy as an average over many origins, at the horizon you will use in production, with a scaled metric such as MASE next to seasonal naive. A single train/test split can rank two methods either way by luck.

courseTitle: TLS and PKI in practice
lessonTitle: Certificate authorities, the CA/Browser Forum and ACME
md: Domain validation proves control of a name at one moment, nothing more. Anyone who can control your DNS or your web server's port 80 for a few minutes can get a valid certificate for your domain. That is why CAA, multi-perspective validation and CT monitoring exist.

courseTitle: Triton kernels: block-level GPU programming
lessonTitle: Fused softmax: one row per program, reductions on chip
md: Fusion in Triton is mostly a matter of keeping a tile in registers between operations. Load once, do every elementwise op and reduction on the block, store once.

courseTitle: Unified multimodal models: one transformer that reads and draws
lessonTitle: Evaluating unified models and choosing a design
md: GenEval prompts are short and templated, and some models are trained mostly on long synthetic captions. Emu3's authors say exactly this and report rewriter numbers too. Before comparing two papers, check the rewriter, the CFG scale, and whether numbers were measured or copied from another paper.

courseTitle: Unikernels: one application, one address space, one VM image
lessonTitle: Concurrency in one address space: cooperative threads and no fork
md: A unikernel runs many requests on one vCPU by **interleaving at waits**: an event loop or cooperative threads overlap I/O, a long computation blocks everyone, and more cores means **more unikernels**, not more threads.

courseTitle: Vector database internals: SIMD kernels, segments and disk
lessonTitle: SIMD distance kernels: lanes, FMA and the horizontal sum
md: SIMD kernels are not bit-identical to the scalar loop. FAISS explicitly allows reassociation in its distance loops; that is a deliberate choice, not a bug. Do not assert exact equality of distances across CPUs or builds.

courseTitle: Vector database internals: SIMD kernels, segments and disk
lessonTitle: Segments: immutable indexes, a write buffer, tombstones and merges
md: Tombstoned vectors are not free. They still occupy memory, and in a graph they are still traversed for routing. Heavy delete or update workloads need merges (and their CPU cost for rebuilding graphs) or latency and memory creep up.

courseTitle: verl: the HybridFlow RL training stack for LLMs
lessonTitle: WorkerGroups, resource pools and DataProto dispatch
md: Do not read `world_size` as the data-parallel size. On 8 GPUs with TP 2 a WorkerGroup has 8 workers but only 4 data shards. Splitting the batch 8 ways would hand different samples to two GPUs that must run the same sharded matmul together.

courseTitle: Video-LLMs with long-video memory
lessonTitle: Which frames to look at: uniform sampling and the needle problem
md: A hit is necessary, not sufficient. A sampled frame inside the event only gives the model a chance; it still has to recognize the content at the token resolution it was given. The formula is an upper bound on what sampling allows.

courseTitle: Virtualization and hypervisor security
lessonTitle: VT-x and AMD-V: VM entries, VM exits and the control structure
md: "There is no software-visible bit whose setting indicates whether a logical processor is in VMX non-root operation," says the SDM. Do not rely on a guest being unable to tell it is virtualised (timing and CPUID reveal it), and never rely on a guest being unable to call your exit handlers with hostile values.

courseTitle: Virtualization and hypervisor security
lessonTitle: Side channels across VMs: what the hypervisor must flush and isolate
md: "We flush on VM entry, so we are safe" is the classic half-fix. A flush protects a moment on one hardware thread. If a sibling thread runs another tenant or the host, the data comes back. Cross-tenant hosts need flushes AND isolation in space: no SMT sharing across trust boundaries.

courseTitle: Fine-tuning a vision model (ViT)
lessonTitle: The recipe: schedule, augmentation, per-layer learning rates
md: Augmentation is a training-time tool. At evaluation use only the checkpoint's deterministic resize, center crop and normalization; random crops or Mixup at test time just add noise to your accuracy estimate.

courseTitle: Visual tokenizers: turning images into discrete tokens
lessonTitle: Why a transformer wants an image as a few discrete tokens
md: A visual tokenizer is to images what BPE is to text: a fixed map from raw input to a short sequence of ids from a finite vocabulary. Unlike BPE it is a learned, lossy neural network, so its reconstruction quality caps how good generated images can look.

courseTitle: vLLM attention backends: selection, batching, KV layout, CUDA graphs
lessonTitle: How vLLM chooses a backend: priority lists and validation
md: Automatic selection takes the first backend in the platform's priority list that passes `validate_configuration`. Explicit selection validates one backend and fails loudly. Neither path guesses.

courseTitle: vLLM attention backends: selection, batching, KV layout, CUDA graphs
lessonTitle: Hybrid models and KV cache groups: one pool, many block tables
md: Hybrid models give each KV cache group its own block table and slot mapping, so the builder runs per attention group and can even be a different backend per group. What stays shared is the pool: one page size, one layout, and kernel blocks when a backend needs smaller ones.

courseTitle: Vision-language models for reading images
lessonTitle: Reading a receipt into validated JSON
md: Validate meaning, not just shape. Documents carry their own checksums: line items sum to a subtotal, subtotal plus tax equals the total, dates fall in a plausible range. Use them.

courseTitle: Wait-free algorithms: bounded progress for every thread
lessonTitle: Herlihy's universal construction: announce, then help
md: Universal does not mean practical. Every cell carries a full object state, and every operation contends on the single end of one log, so operations on different parts of the object (a queue's head and tail) still conflict. Kogan and Petrank point to these two costs, state copying and no disjoint-access parallelism, as why universal constructions are hardly considered practical.

courseTitle: Weather and climate foundation models: GraphCast to Aurora
lessonTitle: Uncertainty: GenCast's diffusion ensembles and CRPS
md: CRPS = accuracy minus half the spread. It rewards ensembles that are both close to the truth and honestly spread, and reduces to absolute error for one forecast.

courseTitle: Web application testing and bug bounty practice
lessonTitle: Testing sessions: tokens, cookie flags, fixation and logout
md: Four session questions: is the token random, is it protected in the browser, is it replaced at login, and does the server forget it at logout? Each has a WSTG ID and a replay you can run with your own account.

courseTitle: Web application testing and bug bounty practice
lessonTitle: Coordinated disclosure: when and how to publish
md: Publish when the rules allow, after deployers can protect themselves, with secrets and other people's data removed. The goal of disclosure is to reduce harm, not to prove you were first.

courseTitle: The browser security model
lessonTitle: HTTPS, mixed content and HSTS: keeping the network out
md: Firesheep's full fix is three layers: **HTTPS on every page** (nothing worth stealing in clear text), **`Secure` cookies** (the session never rides a plain request, even one an attacker tricks the browser into making), and **HSTS** (the browser refuses plain HTTP and certificate click-through for the whole site).

courseTitle: Windows for security: accounts, processes, registry and event logs
lessonTitle: Processes, services and svchost: what runs, and as whom
md: For every unknown process or service ask: which account (token), which file path, which parent, and when was it created? Those four facts come from Task Manager, Get-CimInstance, 4688 and 7045.

courseTitle: Wireless and mobile security
lessonTitle: WPA3: SAE, protected management frames and Enhanced Open
md: SAE moves password guessing from offline (unlimited, invisible) to online (one try per handshake, visible to the AP). PMF stops forged disconnections. OWE encrypts open networks but does not authenticate them. None of them makes a weak password strong against online guessing.

courseTitle: Wireless and mobile security
lessonTitle: Zero-click attacks: from Trident to the Pixel 9 chain
md: Zero-click attack surface is every parser that runs on attacker-supplied data before the user acts. New convenience features (previews, transcription, search) add parsers. Defence is architectural: fewer and memory-safe parsers, tight sandboxes, unreachable drivers, and short patch times.

courseTitle: WSD learning-rate schedules
lessonTitle: Why the loss plunges during the decay: the river valley picture
md: A lower LR does not remove the hill instantly: the walls only pull the iterate down while it still takes steps of reasonable size. That is why the cooldown needs a minimum length. MiniCPM found a 2.5% decay falls short where 10% suffices.

courseTitle: Zero-copy I/O: sendfile, splice and MSG_ZEROCOPY
lessonTitle: splice and tee: pipes as buffers of page references
md: Pipes are the kernel's zero-copy buffer: slots of reference-counted page pointers. splice moves those pointers between a pipe and any descriptor, tee duplicates them, and sendfile itself runs on this machinery with a hidden internal pipe.

courseTitle: Zero-shot classification: labels chosen at inference time
lessonTitle: Prompting an LLM and calibrating its label bias
md: Constrain the LLM to the label set, read a probability per label, and divide by the probabilities a content-free input gets under the same prompt. Calibration fixes a constant shift; it cannot fix a model that does not understand the labels.
